reply.text:
Grip giving out before your back does is common, and it's a training problem we can fix. A few things help:

1. Dead hangs. Hang from the bar for time a few times a week, and build up the seconds slowly.
2. Hand position. Wrap your thumb around the bar and squeeze it hard from the start, rather than hanging on with your fingertips. The hook should sit deep in the palm.
3. Chalk, if your gym allows it. It makes a big difference for sweaty hands.
4. Heavy carries. Farmer's carries or heavy dumbbell holds at the end of a session build grip without much extra fatigue.
5. Run grip work after your pulling, not before, so your pull-up sets stay fresh.

If you can still get reps but your hands are the limit, stop the set there and rest. Grinding on a failing grip just wears you out and teaches sloppy reps.

If you want, I can add farmer's carries or dead hangs to your program.
